title: Generalized Fidelity and the Data Processing Inequality
abstract: In this note, we show that the generalized Bures--Wasserstein distance induced by the generalized fidelity does not satisfy the data processing inequality in dimensions greater than two. In dimension two, although we do not settle the DPI in full generality, we derive two sufficient conditions guaranteeing it by using an explicit formula for the real part of the generalized fidelity. Furthermore, we find a necessary and sufficient condition under which the generalized fidelity reduces to the Uhlmann fidelity.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the generalized Bures--Wasserstein distance derived from the generalized fidelity, finding that it generally violates the Data Processing Inequality in dimensions higher than two. For qubits, the authors provide specific conditions under which the DPI holds, offering deeper insights into the robustness of quantum distance measures under noisy quantum channels.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the generalized Bures--Wasserstein distance, induced by the generalized fidelity, satisfies the Data Processing Inequality (DPI) for quantum channels.
main_result: The distance fails to satisfy the DPI in dimensions greater than two, but sufficient conditions for the DPI are derived for the two-dimensional (qubit) case.
method: The authors use explicit formulas for the generalized fidelity, Pauli matrix representations, and construct counterexamples using block matrices to test the DPI.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum states represented by positive semi-definite matrices, particularly in the qubit case (2x2 matrices), and their evolution under quantum channels.
key_observables: Generalized Fidelity (FR), Squared generalized Bures--Wasserstein distance (BR), and Uhlmann fidelity (Fu).
important_parameters: Dimensionality ($n \geq 2$), and the specific structure of the quantum channels ($\Phi$).
main_assumptions: For the qubit case, the analysis relies on specific algebraic properties derived from the structure of the fidelity and the assumption of specific relationships between fidelities.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the non-satisfaction of DPI for $n \geq 3$. It then derives sufficient conditions for the DPI in $n=2$ using explicit formulas. Finally, it analyzes the relationship between the generalized fidelity and the Uhlmann fidelity, and examines the DPI failure using channel operations.
why_interesting: The study of distance metrics and their monotonicity under quantum operations (like channels) is fundamental to understanding quantum information capacity and process fidelity, making it highly relevant to quantum information theory.
